Question 11
?
Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (2+x)9 in ascending powers of x to approximate (1.98)9. Round your answer to three decimal places.
(1.98)9≈
467.763
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The binomial theorem for positive integer n states that (a+b)n=(n0)anb0+(n1)an−1b1+(n2)an−2b2+…+(nn)a0bn.

By substituting a=2, b=x, and n=9, we obtain (2+x)9=(90)(2)9(x)0+(91)(2)9−1(x)1+(92)(2)9−2(x)2+⋯=1(2)9+9(2)8x+36(2)7x2+⋯=512+9(256)x+36(128)x2+⋯=512+2304x+4608x2+⋯.

So, for small x, we have (2+x)9≈512+2304x+4608x2.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.02 into the above approximation of (2+x)9: (1.98)9=(2+(−0.02))9≈512+2304(−0.02)+4608(−0.02)2=512+2304(−0.02)+4608(0.0004)=512−46.08+1.8432≈467.763, rounded to three decimal places.
